Extension of NREGS benefits to farming community 
*521.      SHR1 B.J, PANDAS-MS. 
MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government proposes to extend National Rural Employment Guarantee Schenu 
NREGS) benefits to the farming community; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
†† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri B.J  Panda  

2    Oral Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
(c)  whether Government proposes to grant labour subsidy to the farmers to work on their 
own fields to help control migration from rural areas and to address their distress; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRIRAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH): 
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) and (b) NREGA is demand based. The Act provides a le gal guarantee of 100 days of 
employment to every rural household in a financial year whose adult members volunteer to. , do 
unskilled manual work. Thus, all rural households including the farming community may benefit 
under NREGA if they register and obtain job cards and apply for doing unskilled manual work. 
Para l(iv) of Schedule I of the Act provides for pr ovision of irrigation facility, horticulture 
plantation and land development facilities on land owned by hous eholds belonging to the 
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes or to Below Poverty Line families or to beneficiaries of 
land reforms or to the beneficiaries under the Indira Awas Yojana of the Government of India. 
(c) and (d): No such proposal is under consideration of thi s Ministry. NREGA woks are 
taken up on the public land. However, para 1 (iv) of Sched ule I of the NREG Act stipulates 
works to be carried out on the individual land as detailed in reply to Part (a) & (b) of the 
Question. Wages to the unskilled labourers working on all projects taken up under NREGA . 
 are entirely borne by the Central Government. 
SHRI B.J. PANDA: Sir, even last year, in the deliberations on this issue, this matter had 
been raised by many hon. Members that the NREG Scheme be made applicable to farmers 
who are tilling their own land and the hon. Minister, even last year, had not referred to this 
issue. In today's reply, which is laid on the Table of the House, it has been stated that the 
Scheme is eligible for farmers who are in the SC/ST category and the BPL farmers who own 
their own land. We know that it is already applicable to SC/ST categories. But, we are talking 
about the other categories OBC, General and other poor farmers. But, there is an anomaly 
here. If it is applicable only to farmers who are BPL but own land, then there is a contradiction. 
I am sure, the hon. Minister will appreciate. Farmers who o wn land", normally, do not come ' 
under the BPL category. They will be above the poverty line. We are talking about the large 
number of farmers who are, actually, BPL and desperately need this facility and who do not 
own  their  own land.   
MR. CHAIRMAN: You put your question. 
SHRI B.J. PANDA: Sir, my supplementary is: Will the hon. Minister consider making this 
Scheme applicable to farmers who are in distress and do not own land to prevent large-scale 
migration from States like Orissa.

MS. MABEL REBELLO: Sir, I would like to know whether the Government proposes to 
establish a technical expert group, as recommended by Dr.  M.S. Swaminathan, so that 
small and marginal farmers, who are definitely below poverty level, can creat permanent 
assets, such as, water harvesting, wells and ponds for i rrigation, horticulture, land 
development, etc. in their own land. In the reply, the h on. Minister has said that 
schedule 1 of the Act provides the provision for all these fa cilities for Below Poverty 
Line families. And, since these small and marginal far mers definitely fall in the category 
of the BPL families, I would like to know what he proposes to do.

agriculture for their livelihood. I would like to know from the hoo. Minister, through you, Sir, how 
many persons have been provided employment under this Act in the last two years. This Act was 
passed two years back by Parliament. The hon. Minister may please reply to this first.

6   Oral Answers;  [RAJYASABHA]  to Questions  
Management support to rural development programmes  
 
 
†*522. DR. T. SUBBARAMIREDDY: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state:  
 whether Government has introduced management suppor t to rural development 
programmes and strengthening of district planning process from financial year 2007-08; 
 whether the scheme primarily focuses on training an d skill development of rural 
development functionaries and members of Panchayati Raj Institutions in rural development 
at Centre, State and district/block level by provid ing financial support to State Institutes of 
Rural Development and Extension Training Centres; 
 if so, whether Government proposes to create awaren ess amongst targeted groups of 
rural development programmes and mobilize them towa rds participatory development 
programme sensitizing opinion making; and 
 if so, the extent of the scheme's implementation and helpfulness? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI RAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH): 
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
 Yes, Sir. From 2007-08, the Government has introduc ed the Head of 'Management 
Support to Rural Development Programmes and Strengthening of District Planning Process' 
having an allocation of Rs. 68 crore. Till 2006-07, the Department of Rural Development was 
having five Central Sector Schemes namely, (i) Moni toring Mechanism, (ii) Information 
Education and Communication (IEC), (iii) Informatio n Technology, (iv) International 
Cooperation and (v) Organisation of Training Courses, Seminars and Workshops. A Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme of Strenthening of State Institute s of Rural Development/Extension 
Training Centres (SIRDs/ETCs) was also being implem ented. For the year 2006-07, total 
allocation of Rs. 68 crore was made for the above s chemes. During the Eleventh Five Year 
Plan discussion, in accordance with the advise of t he Planning Commission these Central 
Sector Schemes, having very small allocations, were  clubbed together under one Head to 
have greater flexibility. 
 Yes, Sir. One of the components of the Management S upport to Rural Development 
Programmes is strengthening of State Institutes of Rural Development/Extension Training 
Centres (SIRDs/ETCs) which focuses on imparting training, information and skill development of 
rural development functionaries and members of Panc hayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). The 
SIRDs are State level institutions for imparting tr aining to trainers and senior level 
development functionaries and elected representatives of the PRIs at the District level. The 
Extension Training Centres (ETCs) function at the r egional level and impart training to 
Village/Block Level rural development functionaries and elected representatives of PRIs at 
Village and Block level. There are 28 SIRDs and 89 ETCs in the country. An amount of 
Rs. 26.55 crore was released during 2007-08 for conducting 15283 training programmes for 
659639 participants.  
 and (d) For creation of awareness among targeted groups, funding is provided under 
the second major IEC component of Management Suppor t Services to rural development 
programmes. The IEC activities aim at dissemination  of information about the rural 
development programmes amongst the stakeholders to create awareness among the 
beneficiaries about their rights and the processes involved for getting benefits and also

endeavour for their all round development and skill upgradation and provide know how on 
different aspects to help in capacity building. It also ai ms to educate the functionaries of 
PRIs at various levels about the processes of implementat ion of Rural Development 
Programmes etc. The effort is made to sensitize the opinion makers, NGOs and representatives 
of the people regarding the issues relating to rural development. All these efforts are made 
to promote participatory approach for the rural development programmes. After launching 
of National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS), the IEC activities have been 
carried out in a more focused manner involving the concerned  district authorities so that 
adequate awareness is created among the rural community. Dur ing the year 2007-08, an 
amount of Rs. 18 crore was spent. 
Monitoring mechanism is another component which has been clubbed  with the 
Management Support Services for rural development programmes. The Ministry of Rural 
Development has a multi-tool monitoring system through which the implementation of rural 
development programmes is closely monitored. All expenses incurred on the meetings of 
Performance Review Committee, National Level Monitors,  Evaluation and Concurrent 
Evaluation Studies, Impact Studies and holding of State and District Level Vigilance and 
Monitoring Committees are met from this Head. 
DR. T. SUBBARAMIREDDY: Sir, first of all, I want to congratulate the Rural Development 
Minister, Dr. Raghuvansh Prasad Singhji, for the biggest and lengthiest reply that his 
Ministry has given. 
Sir, the Government has introduced a very noble and innovat ive Scheme called 
management support to rural development programmes and strengthening of district planning 
process. In this connection, I would like to know whether under the Scheme, there is a plan 
also to focus on evolving a comprehensive system for effective monitoring and evaluation 
of various rural development programmes through periodical progr ess reports, annual 
conferences, workshops and seminars and inspection through field visits by senior officers 
of the Rural Development Ministry, besides carrying out in -depth studies in the form of 
concurrent evaluation and impact assessment studies through r eputed and independent 
research organisations to ascertain the impact of these p rogrammes. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Question, please. 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: Sir, I would also like to know whether the programme 
includes scheme for rural training. If so, what are the c oncrete measures that have been 
so far initiated and to what extent this will help in remo ving the hurdles and inordinate 
delays in implementing the various schemes concerning rural development?

DR. T. SUBBARAMIREDDY: Sir, it is a very big task to implement the National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Programme in all the 596 rural districts in the country. Here I would 
like to know whether, in a move to assess the impact of its ambitious programme under the 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, the Government ha s decided to rope students 
from the Universities and premier institutions, including IIMs and IITs, to scientifically 
study the implementation of the Scheme and give their feedbacks . 
If so, whether in this regard the Minister has already wri tten letters to universities and 
institutions suggesting them to incorporate the Scheme as  part of their rural management 
course. 
Sir, I would also like to know... 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Just one question, please. 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: Sir, just one second, please. I want to know what are the 
steps taken to see that there is no misappropriation of funds in i mplementing the Scheme, 
and, to what extent, the Scheme has helped in improving the economic condition of the rural 
people. I also want to know what are the concrete measures taken to implement the Scheme 
in 596 districts in future.

SHRIMATIJAYANTHINATARAJAN: Sir, I would like to thank the hon. Minister for the 
detailed reply. We know that over ten lakh women have been elected to the local bodies in 
the country. This is one of our greatest achievements at the level of local Government. The 
most important hurdle that the women elected representat ives face is the lack of training 
and the lack of information at the level of the Panchayati  Raj Institutions. So, my specific 
question to the hon. Minister would be, he has said that out of the 89 ETCs and 28 SIRDs, 
we have spent Rs. 26 crores on 15,000 training programmes for nearly 66,000 people from the 
Panchayati Raj institutions; does the Minister have any information on how many women 
were there? The second part of my question is, are there any women-oriented training

rogrammes, because the problems that the women repr esentatives in the Panchayats face—and they 
have said so at many fora— are very different from what the men face at some levels. Are there any

make more Extension Training Centres, because 89 Ex tension Training Centres for a country of the 
size of India is really too small.

Designing of software by TCS on NREG programme  
*523. SHRIMATIVIPLOVE THAKUR: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 
 whether it is a fact that a specially designed software h as been prepared by Tata 
Consultancy Service Social Sector team, which helps in tra cking every detail in NREGA 
Scheme; 
 whether it is also a fact that this software has been su ccessfully used in Andhra 
Pradesh to prevent misuse of funds meant for implementation of NREGA Scheme; 
 if so, the details of the said software; and 
 what steps Government propose to take to use this software i n the entire country? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRIRAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH): 
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (d) Government of Andhra Pradesh with the help of T ata Consultancy Services, 
(TCS), has developed a software for the Government of Andh ra Pradesh to monitor the 
State Government's implementation of NREGS in the State. As reported by Government of 
Andhra Pradesh, this software has enabled the State Governm ent to elicit data on the 
implementation of the programme in Andhra Pradesh as per the State Government's 
requirement. However, the TCS software used by the Government of Andhra Pradesh does 

Oral Answers  [30 APRIL 2008]  to Questions    11 
not capture data on critical statutory parameters such as the date of registration, household 
photograph on the Job Card, employment application date, dated, receipt against 
employment demand, daily attendance on muster rolls. Government of Andhra Pradesh has 
been advised to prepare a bridge software so that its TC S software may be enabled to 
generate data on National templates of the Ministry of Rural Development's website. 
NREGA is a National Act and programme and the data has to be captured on standardized 
comprehensive parameters which are applicable across the country and subserve the non-
negotiable statutory requirements of the Act. As such, the M inistry has already through 
NIC developed the National Software for NREGA, viz. nregasoft. The NIC software supports 
the operation of the computer based Management Information System (MIS) for NREGA, 
www.nrega.nic.in  at the transaction level. It has been carefully designed, ke eping in view 
the statutory requirements of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act. It enables a 
detailed household based tracking of all physical and financial aspects of implementation. 
It places all data in public domain and infuses transparency in programme implementation. 
It also generates analytical reports and alerts for States to closely monitor the processes of 
the Act and fund utilization. The NIC software for NREGA has won awards, viz., (a) Microsoft 
e-Governance Award, 2006 (b) Skoch Challenger Award, 2007 (c) Dataquest e-Governance 
Champion Award, 2008. 
All the States are already using the NIC software with the exception of Andhra Pradesh. 
In a two-day National Workshop on MIS for NREGA on 28-29, December, 2007 all States IT 
Teams confirmed the high quality of the national software of NREGA built by NIC in the 
Ministry of Rural Development. 
The MIS software developed by the Ministry has been through N IC, a Government 
organization. The software is fully owned by the Ministry and its maintenance is cost 
effective. It serves the purposes of the National Act in a ll its parameters. In contrast, the 
TCS software being used by Government of Andhra Pradesh has  been developed by a 
private sector organization that retains the copyright fo r it. The maintenance of the TCS 
software is costlier, and information on all aspects of NREGA is not captured by it. Therefore, 
the question of using TCS software in the entire country does not ar ise.

Inspection Report of Admiral Gorshkov  
†525. SHRI M.V. MYSURAREDDY: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state: 
 whether the inspection of Admiral Gorshkov which was to be completed by March, 
2008 is over; 
 if so, the details of inspection report; 
 whether it is a fact that Russia has made it clear to the Ministry that cost escalation of 
Admiral Gorshkov is a must; and 
 if so, what is the price escalation Russia has proposed and to what extent Government 
has agreed to give? 
* 524. [The question (s) Shri Shahid Siddiqui was absent. For answer vide page .........Infra] 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI A.K. ANTONY): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (d) The Russian side submitted a revised Master Schedule indicating a delay in the 
project and an increase in price for repair and re-equipping of  aircraft carrier ex-Admiral 
Gorshkov. The Russian side has indicated revision in time and cost due to 'Growth of Work'. 
The price escalation proposed by the Russian side is US Dollar 1202 million. The process of 
examination of the scope and necessity for additional work pr ojected by the Russian side 
has been initiated. 
SHRI M. V. MYSURA REDDY: Sir, as per the Minister's reply, the escalation proposal by 
Russia for completion of Gorshkov is 1,202 million US dollars. This is nothing but breach of 
contract. When the contract was signed, it was a fixed-price contract and there is no clause 
for renegotiation in the agreement. Now, Russia is saying that  substantial price rise is 
inescapable and we are examining on this which does not exist at all in the original contract.

ILO Report on unemployment forecast  
*529. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 whether the International Labour Organization (ILO) in its recent report has revealed 
that there will be unemployment of estimated 5 million in 2008; 
 if so, the likely unemployment in India as per the said report; 
 whether the unemployment rate in the country is increasing alarmingly and the steps 
taken by Government to provide jobs have not proved effective; and 
(d) if so, the strategies to be adopted to face the chal lenges of unemployment in the 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SHRI OSCAR FERN ANDES): (a) The Report of Global Employment Trends, January, 2008 
released by the International Labour Organisation has predicted that overall employment in 
the world is expected to increase by around 40 million in 2008 and unemployment could 
further increase by 5 million. This would lead to a slight increase of unemployment rate to 
6.1 percent. 

24   Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Starred Questions  
 No separate data on unemployment in India has been given in the Report. However, 
the Report has indicated that for the time being South Asia to which India is a part, still has 
an enormous deficit in decent work; too many people are in vulnerable employment situations 
and too many are working and still living in poverty. But, there are hopeful signs; people are 
moving out of agriculture sector to work in more productive sectors; extreme working 
poverty is decreasing tremendously; unemployment remains at low levels, and, productivity 
growth is leading to productivity levels that may soon be sufficiently high to yield wages 
high enough to take people out of US$2 a day working poverty. 
 and (d) As per the two most recent quinquennial rounds of National Sample Survey 
Organisation (NSS)) reports on employment and unemployment, unemployment rate on 
Current Daily Status basis has been estimated at 7.31 % in 1999-2000 (55th round) and 8.28% 
in 2004-05 (61st round). The employment opportunities were estimated at 33 8.19 million in 
1999-2000 (55th round) and 384.91 million in 2004-05 (61st round). 
The Eleventh Five Year Plan provides a frame-work to restructure policies to achieve a 
new vision based on faster, more broad-based and more inclusive growth. It aims at making 
employment generation an integral part of the growth process and devising strategies to 
accelerate not only growth of employment but also for wages of the poorly paid. The 
Eleventh Plan document approved by National Development Council has projected that 58 
million job opportunities on Current Daily Status are likely to be created during the Eleventh 
Plan period. Besides, Government of India is implementing various employment generation 
and poverty alleviation programmes in both rural and urban areas to increase employment 
opportunities. Some of the important ones are-Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY); 
Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana (PMRY); Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY); 
Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP); Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) 
and National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA), 2005.  
Steps have been initiated to identify and implement systematic reforms in administration 
of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) so as to facilitate closer interaction with the industry 
in order to improve quality of training, make the graduates better employable and help them 
earn  decant wages.

*534.     SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
SHRI VIJAYJ.DARDA: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 whether the National Bomb Centre of National Security Guard prepared a database on 
the basis of threat perception to protect our key security installations and economic hubs, 
with primary focus to save lives; 
 if so, whether security experts have emphasized greater need of carrying out periodic 
security audits of such places; and 
 whether a system of intelligence sharing of time and loc ation of possible attacks 
amongst countries which have established anti-terrorist ce lls has been evolved?

and the" Security agencies, to study the trends in the unla wful use of explosives and

Steps taken by the Government to strengthen the textile i ndustry  
 In order to facilitate modernization/Technology Upgradation  of Textiles mills, 
Government have launched Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme for Te xtile and 
Jute Industries w.e.f. 1.4.1999 for a period of 5 years which was subsequently extended 
up to 31.3.2007 and stands extended during Eleventh Five Year Plan (w.e.f. 01-11-07) 
with special thrust on garmenting, technical textiles and processing segments. Under 
TUFS 10990 units with a project cost of Rs. 86,026.45 crore have been sanctioned an 
amount of Rs. 36,950.11 crore as on 31.03.2007. Out of this Rs. 27,448.86 crore have 
been disbursed to 10216 units as on 31.03.2007. Under TUFS, an option has been 
provided to the Small Scale Textile and Jute Industries t o avail of either 15% Credit 
Linked Capital Subsidy (CLCS) or the existing 5% interest reimbursement under the 
TUFS. An additional option has been given to powerloom units w.e.f. the 6th November, 
2003 to avail of 20% capital subsidy under TUF Scheme. Modifications in technology 
and financial norms of the scheme are being made on a continuous basis to make the 
scheme more industry friendly. The Government has approved additional 10% capital 
subsidy for specified processing machinery under TUFS, w.e.f. 20/4/2005.

Protest against films passed by Censor Board 
3948. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR: Will the Minister of  INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
 whether Government is aware of the increasing number of protests, which often turn 
violent, against the screening of certain films des pite the fact that they have been passed 
by the Censor Board; 
 whether it reflects poorly on the functioning of the Censor Board; and 
 what steps Government proposes to take to ensure that the certification given by the 
Censor Board is acceptable to all communities? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI PRIYARANJAN  
DASMUNSI): (a) Yes, Sir. Media reports have indicat ed that there had been protests in 
some States against certian films despite -their be ing certified by Central Board of Film 
Certification (CBFC). 
 No, Sir. CBFC certifies films in  accordance with the Cinematograph Act, 1952 and 
Rules and Guidelines framed thereunder. 
 CBFC has its headquarters at Mumbai. Its nine regio nal officers are located at 
Bangalore, Calcutta, Chennai, Cuttack, Guwahati, Hy derabad, Mumbai, New Delhi and 
Tbiruvananthapuram which cater to the films imported into or produced in their respective 
jurisdictional areas. The regional offices are assisted in the examination of films by advisory 
panels (constituted under Section 5 of the Cinematograph Act) consisting of persons from 
different walks of life. 
Additionally, as per Rule 41(4)(c) of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 1983, in 
cases where the members of the Examining Committee, after the examination of the film, 
submit to the Chairman a provisional report indicat ing that expert opinion on subjects 
depicted in the film such as subjects relating to defence or foreign relations or any particular 
religion or law or medicine or any other subject, should be sought before the final report is 
submitted, the Chairman may after taking into consideration the circumstances of the case 
specify a time limit for obtaining the expert opinion and for the submission of the final report 
of the Examining Committee thereafter.

3970. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be 
pleased to state: 
 whether Government has decided to form a Committee to check the child labour 
charges reported in the leading newspaper London that an international clothing brand has

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) to (c) No, Sir. However, Government has taken a series of 
steps for elimination of child labour from export oriented industries. This includes various 
measures taken by the export promotion councils to eliminate use of child labour and also 
the awareness and monitoring programmes conducted b y the Export Promotion Councils 
for the purpose. Government of India has taken up t his issue of use of child labour in the 
export-oriented industries with all the Indian Emba ssies/High Commissions abroad to 
sensitize them on the issue of child labour and their possible impact. Government has also 
taken up this matter with various trade councils to ensure that no child labour is employed 
by the member exporters. Further, the steps taken b y the Government in the carpet sector 
also inplude regular surveillance on child labour u ndertaken by a professional agency, 
setting up of National Level Steering Committee, formulation of a code of conduct for the

Ensuring quality roads under PMGSY in  Jharkhand  
3978. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased 
to state: 
(a) by when all the tribal hamlets of 1000 families will be connected by Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) in Jharkhand; 
 whether the PMGSY roads in Jharkhand meet the quali ty norms of Government of 
India; 
 whether Government is aware that PMGSY works are su b-contracted number of 
times and hence sub-standard quality roads are constructed in Jharkhand; and 
 in what way Government propose to ensure quality in PMGSY? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI 
SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) 'Rural Roads' has been identified as one of the six components 
of 'Bharat Nirman' with a goal to provide connectiv ity to all habitations with a population 
of 1000 persons and above (500 persons and above in the case of hilly or tribal areas) will 
an all-weather road by 2009. The Government of Jharkhand has informed that road works 
sanctioned under Pradhan Marntri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Phase I and II have been 
completed. Construction of roads under Phase III and IV are in progress. Under Phase V of 
PMGSY, proposals have been cleared to connect 369 hamlets of more than 1000 population 
for which tenders have been finalized. The State Government has indicated that the works 
under Phase V are likely to be completed by May, 20 09. After clearance of Phase V 
proposals, 502 habitations having a population of 1000 or more will still remain unconnected. 
It has been indicated by the State Government that the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for 
providing connectivity to these 502 habitations are under preparation. 
 Roads under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) are constructed as per 
specifications applicable for rural roads and as pe r the provisions in Rural Roads Manual 
IRC SP: 20 prepared by Indian Roads Congress (IRC). 
 'Rural Roads' is a State subject. Projects under PM GSY are executed by State/UT 
Governments through their agencies. State Executing  Agency award the works as per 
Standard Bidding Document (SBD). There is a provisi on for sub-contracting in SBD. 
Ensuring the quality of the road works is the responsibility of the State Government who is 
implementing the programme. NRRDA has issued genera l guidelines on quality control 
and prescribed a Quality Assurance Handbook to regulate quality control process at works 
level. Proposals for sub-contracting has not been received under PMGSY works. 
(d) Under PMGSY, a three-tier Quality Control mecha nism is envisaged. State 
Governments are responsible for the first two tiers  of the quality control structure. The 
Programme Implementation Units (PIUs) is the first tier, whose primary responsibility is to 
ensure that all the materials utilized and the work manship conform to the prescribed 
specifications. The PIU supervises the site quality control laboratory set up by the contractor. 
It also ensures that all the test prescribed are carried out at the specified time and place by 
the specified person/authority. Thus, as per Guidelines all the works under the PMGSY are 
tested for quality of material and workmanship by the implementing agency. Under second 

Written Answers to  [30 APRIL 2008]  Unstarred Questions    141 
tier of quality management, the State Government is  required to deploy State Quality 
Monitors (SQMs) for monitoring of quality of road w orks under the programme. In the 
third tier of quality mechanism, National Rural Roa ds Develoment Agency (NRRDA) is 
engaging independent National Quality Monitors (NQM s) for monitoring of quality of 
raod works on random basis. Since inception upto December, 2007, 1081 inspections have

ELANGOVAN): (a) The Textiles trade bodies and assoc iations have represented that the 
appreciation of the rupee vis-a-vis US dollar during 2007, has adversely affected the exports 
of textiles and clothing from India. However, trade statistics available for the period April-
December, 2007 indicate that the overall exports at  USD 14935.69 million in this period 
denotes an increase of 9.33% in US dollar terms, over the corresponding period of 2006-07,

 As per estimates made by Confederation of India Textile Industry (CITI), for every

industry, which has been representing that textile exports have been affected by the 
appreciation of the value of rupee vis-a-vis the US Dollar. These measures include the

port services for exports, transport of goods by road from container depot to port 
of export, general insurance services for insurance of goods for export, technical 
testing and analysis agency services and inspection and certification services, 
storage & warehousing services and clearing activity services.  
(vii) Customs duty on intermediates for Polyester staple fibre and polyester filament 
yarn reduced from 7.5% to 5%.  
(viii) Customs duty on paraxylene, a raw material for the intermediate PTA reduced from 
2%t0%.  
(ix) Customs duty reduced on other man-made filament yarn & staple fibres of acrylic 
& viscose from 10% to 5%.  
(x) Customs duty reduced on spun yarn of man-made staple fibres & filament yarn 
(other than nylon) from 10% to 5%.  
(xi) Customs duty reduced on polyester chips from 7.5% to 5%.

Request to regularise services of Casual workers of BSNL in Orissa 
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA (Orissa): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, I thank you very much for 
giving me this opportunity to raise an issue relati ng to the casual labourers of BSNL in 
Orissa who are still to be regularised. Inspite of the fact that they have served as casual labour 
for a long time in different units of BSNL in Orissa they are still to be regularised and they are 
to be counted as employees. The total number of these casual labourers is about 1500. They 
have been demanding it for a long time and the BSNL Office in Delhi has also sent directions 
to Orissa BSNL in this regard to regularise them and settle their problems. This direction was 
given in 2003 but their problems are yet to be settled. Sir, most of the casual labourers belong 
to the SC/ST and Backward Castes. Most of them are from my district of Mayurbhanj. Last 
time the TDM had recommended only 21 cases to the BSNL. Orissa Circle for regularisation 
and out of that only 4 persons were regularised. Lastly, they have taken shelter of the court 
and the court has also directed the BSNL to regularise them and settle their problems. Their 
lives are under stress and their future is uncertain. My submission, through you, Sir, to the 
Minister is that inspite of the intervention of the court and direction from the Delhi Office of 
BSNL the SC/ST/ OBCs casual labourers of BSNL in Orissa in general and casual labourers of 
my district Mayurbhanj in particular who are also living below poverty line are regularised 
immediately. The directions given by the court and the Delhi BSNL should be obeyed by 
the Orissa BSNL as well its district units. Thank you very much. 
SHRIPYARIMOHAN MOHAPATRA (Orissa): Sir, I associate myself with the submission 
made by the hon. Member. 
Dismay over Reported statement by Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare against 
people of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh for spreading diseases

Reservation for Dalit Muslims and Dalit Christians in the Country  
SHRISYED AZEEZ PASHA (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, I want to raise a very important issue 
in mis august House regarding the discrimination of Muslim Dalits and Chrisitian Dalits. Sir, 
right from 1936 they were availing SC status. Unfortunately, by the repugnant para 3 of the 
Presidential Order 1950, they were de-listed from Scheduled Caste category. Later on, in the 
year 1956, Dalits among Sikh community and in 1990, Buddhists, were re-listed once again 
through amendments. It was really a welcome step. B ut, the same facility was denied to 
Muslim Dalits who constitute only 0.80 per cent of the entire Muslim population in India as 
per Rajinder Sachar Committee Report Sir, the denial and deprivation to Muslim and Christian 

Matters Raised  [30 APRIL 2008]  with Permission    169 
Dalits go contrary to the Fundamental Right and basic spirit of the Constitution. Article 14 
speaks equality before law and article 15 clearly mentions about non-discrimination on the 
grounds of religion to any citizen. So, the denial and discrimination is a clear-cut violation 
of the basic tenets and the spirit of Constitution.  While Article 16 emphasises equal 
opportunities in public employment but unfortunately, Muslim Dalits and Christian Dalits 
are not equally treated on par with other SC communities. So to undo the long done injustice 
to these communities, I strongly urge upon the Gove rnment to immediately amend the 
Constitution and re-enlist Muslim Dalits and Christian Dalits in SC category and implement 
the true spirit of articles 14,15,16 and article 20. Thank you.

Kehabilitation-Cum-Revivai package of Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Chairman Sir, I would like to 
raise a very important issue regarding the Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam. It is 
a very prestigious shipyard in the public sector. In fact, the people of India are so proud of 
the greatest contribution made by this shipyard to the shipping industry for so many years. 
But, unfortunately, about 7-8 years ago, when the s hipping industry was in recession, 
nationally and internationally, the Hindustan Shipy ard was in trouble, financially. Now, I 
would like to place before this august House as the  matter stands today. The company has 
incurred Rs. 1106 crores loss in the last three yea rs. The net worth is Rs. 950 crores. With 
the result, even though it has orders in hand for R s. 1956 crores, it is not able to proceed 
further in spite of having high technology, quality of work, manpower, etc., because of lack 
of working capital. 

Matters Raised  [30 APRIL 2008]  with Permission    171 
Recently, the BRPSE recommended to the Government t hat about Rs.950 crores 
should be given for rehabilitation and financial re structuring of this company. 
Subsequently, a Group of Ministers was constituted for which Shri Pranab Mukherjee 
was the Chairman and Shri Chidambaram, the hon. Def ence Minister and the hon. 
Minister for Shipping, Road Transport and Highways were Members. After that, Sir, 
several meetings took place. We understand that it was discussed and decided, 
considering the importance of this shipyard and its  contribution and requirement to the 
Ministry of Defence, particularly for the Indian Na vy, since it has its base at 
Visakhapatnam, by the GoM to handover the shipyard to the Defence Ministry and use it 
for national security purpose. It is a welcome move . On 6th November, 2007, we read in 
newspapers that they have decided to transfer this shipyard to the Ministry of Defence, 
today, we are in April, 2008, but nothing has happe ned so far. The workers unions and 
employeed are all concerned. So many people, who ha d sought voluntary retirement, 
have not got wages, salaries, compensation, etc. I would like to draw the attention of the 
House, the Ministry and aslo the Chairman towards t his very important matter. When the 
Group of Ministers has already decided that they mu st take an immediate decision in the 
matter within thirty days and see to it that all th e concerns of the employees are 
immediately addressed to, then, why there is delay.  The people are very much upset. 
Nation's one of the most prestigious shipyard cannot be treated like this. 
Compulsory Compassionate Appointment for the Dependents of Government Servants

172    Special  [RAJYASABHA]  Mentions  
Demand for granting Indian Citizenship to  Pakistani Passport Holders in Kerala  
SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN (Kerala): Sir, I would like to draw the attention of the 
Government, through this House, to the problem of nearly 300 Kerala people, who 
have submitted applications for Indian citizenship. Nearly 300 Pakistani passport 
holders, who had returned to Kerala at differen points of time, and who are staying 
here under the long-term visa, have submitted appli cations for Indian citizenship. 
They are all staying here for more than 25 years. These poor people, who had gone to 
Pakistan for trade and employment, have no connection with Pakistan. The Government 
of Pakistan is also not ready to accept them. They are all staying here with their kith 
and kin. They were born in Kerala; their parents were Indian citizens; their wives are 
Indian citizens; their children are Indian citizens. Most of them are in the age group of 
late sixties and seventies. They are very poor people. Most of them are bedridden. 
Their situation is very pathetic. Sir, they are demanding for Indian citizenship. They 
have backing from all the political parties of Kerala. When Shri A.K. Antony was the 
Chief Minister of Kerala, he took up this issue with the Central Government and the 
present Government is also supporting their cause. They have all submitted 
applications for citizenship. All the necessary formalities have been completed. I met 
the State Government officials also. They have assured that the State Government 
will give all the support and will recommend for gi ving citizenship to these poor 
people. At the fag end of their life, their only intention is not to die in the no-man's 
land. They would like to die as Indian citizens. They are all born and brought up in 
this country. But, because of socio-economic backwa rdness of this country, they 
were forced to go to Pakistan for employment. Now, they are all here. It is a pathetic 
issue. So, I would request the Government to take up this issue. What is happening in 
Rajasthan and Gujarat is this. In similar cases, in  Gujarat, 1469 people had got 
citizenship, and in Rajasthan 211 people got their citizenship. Unfortunately, people 
living in Kerala did not get it. So, I urge upon th e Government to take necessary 
steps and grant them Indian citizenship.  
SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT (West Bengal): Sir, I associate myself with the matter 
raised by the hon. Member.  
SHRI MATILAL SARKAR (Tripura): Sir, I also associate myself with the matter raised by 
the hon. Member.  
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN (West Bengal): Sir, I also associate myself with it.

SPECIAL MENTIONS  
Concern over poor implementation of the constitutional provisions meant for 
ScheduledCastes in the Country  
SHRI PRAYTiENRASHTRAPAL(Gujarat): Sir, theMinistryof is the Model 
Ministry on issues Concerning the Scheduled Castes at the Central Government level. 
However, the Constitutional rights of this sector are challenged by various forces and the 
Ministry is not giving adequate attention and consideration to the victims.  
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in reply to the Rajya Sabha Unstarred 
Question No. 2914, have admitted that during the year 2006, the total number of cases  

Special  [30 APRIL 2008]  Mentions    173 
registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 
1989 were 32,407. As admitted by the Ministry, the State Governments of Punjab, Uttar 
Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana have specified a Court of Session as a Special Court to try 
the offences under the Act. It is a well-known fact that the ratio of acquittal is very high and 
that of conviction is very low. Even the small requirement that investigation of such cases 
should be by police "officer of the rank of Dy. SP and above is not adhered to by the Police 
Department and, hence, the accused are acquitted on technical grounds. There are hundreds 
of backlog vacancies in various Ministries of the Central Government. There are hundreds 
of cases of bogus caste certificates in various Central Ministries. Urgent action is required 
in favour of Scheduled Castes. The specific item fo r providing reservation Act for the 
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the National Common Minimum Programme is 
not being implemented. So, urgent action should be taken by the Minister of Social Justice 
and Empowerment. 
Demand to take effective measures for development of North-Eastern Region  
of the Country  
SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA TAIMUR (Assam): Sir, the pres ent Government has 
taken various measures for the development of the N orth-Eastern Region. Yet, we have 
seen that development is not progressing because the concerned Ministries are not taking due 
interest. Though DONER Ministry is created by the C entral Government, especially to 
speed up the development of the North-Eastern Regio n, but the progress is very slow. In 
2007, the DONER Minister has asked the North-Eastern MPs to submit the schemes of Rs.5 
crores for two projects of their constituency. All North-Eastern MPs accordingly submitted 
schemes to the DONER Ministry. Till now, most of th e schemes were not sanctioned. 
Some of the Rajya Sabha Members have already retired. 
The Railway Ministry in the present Budget sanction ed 10 Garib Rath for the poor 
people with low fare and other facilities, but not a single Garib Rath is provided to the North-
Eastern Region. The Rajdhani Express is running in the North-East. The Rajdhani Express 
has stoppage in major big cities. Small town people  and poor people are not getting its 
benefit. 
Sir, it is seen that while giving appointment to th e unemployed youth in the Central 
Government Corporations and Industries and Railways , unemployed youth of the North-
Eastern Region do not get jobs. Most of the jobs ar e given to youth belonging to other 
States for which there is very much resentment in t he Ass.::n State where unemployed 
youth are increasing in number. Because of unemployment, there is insurgency. So, I request 
the concerned Ministries to take these problems ser iously and eradicate the grievances of 
the North-Eastern Region. 
Demand to grant 'C Class city status to Baripada town in Mayurbhanj, Orissa  
MS. SUSHILATIRIYA(Orissa): Sir, I would like to mention the following matter under 
Rule 180(A) in the House requesting Class 'C city status for Baripada town of Mayurbhanj 
district in the State of Orissa. 
The town of Baripada was the capital of Mayurbhanj State before the merger agreement 
with Government of India in 1948. During that time development work such as irrigation, 
beautification of town with construction work of beautiful palaces, etc. had been carried

out. There are two or three ponds surrounding the town. The town is also a corridor to the 
Similipahar Biosphere Reserve. There are many tourist places surrounding the city such as 
Kichakeswari temple, Sammibrushk and Debakund, which add to the great tourist attraction 
of the district. The population of the city is more than one lakh and forty thousand. It is the 
only Municipality in the district.others are N.A.C. During the Tenth and Eleveth Lok Sabha, 
when I was Member of the Lok Sabha Mayurbanj was declared as the telecom district. The 
facility of Telecom has also been extended to rural areas now. It has a university called the 
North Orissa University. 
Sir, Baripaua town may be declared as a 'C Class ci ty, as has been demanded by the 
public a nu;nber of times in the past, because it h ouses the district headquarters and 
belongs to the thickly populated tribal district of Mayurbhanj in the State of Orissa. 
Demand to provide reservation for women in all areas of Governance 
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK (Goa): Sir, Special Mentions are allowed as per 
rules. But laying them are not as per rules. Sir, we are being discriminated against. What is 
provided under the Rules is not being permitted. 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: It is with the consensus of the House. Please lay it on the 
Table of the House. 
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK  Okay, I will lay it on the Table of the House. 
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK: Sir, giving the women certain reservations by 
reserving seats in the elected bodies or nomination s in the non-elected bodies is gaining 
momentum in the country. 
Former Prime Miniser late Shri Rajiv Gandhi's initiative bore fruits as, his ground work led 
to the passage of 73rd and 74th Amendment Bills to the Constitution of India after his ragic 
demise. The concept will undoubtedly proceed toward s its logical milestone by way of 
women getting, one fine day, representation in Parliament and Stat? Assemblies. 
However, there are several hurdles in getting such a bill passed immediately but, 
comparatively, in areas where there are less hurdles like  executive and judiciary, Government 
should take faster steps. 
It is time that we reserve one-third post for women in the Supreme Court, High Courts, in 
lower judiciary, quasi-judicial and revenue bodies. 
If the concept is for the good of the society, then it should not be restricted to legislatures 
only, but should encompass executive and judiciary too. 
The Union Government can constitute a task force to prepare a blue print, a road map with 
necessary drafts for amending the required legislations/rules, etc., by involving State Governments. 
I think the experiment is worth trying when we are on the threshold of e-governance, a 
system in which there is no scope to differentiate between hard job and soft job. 
Demand for proper Rehabilitation of the people affected in Bhopal Gas Tragedy 
SHRI B.S. GNANADESIKAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I would like to bring to the kind notice of 
this Government the continuous struggle of the peop le who were affected by chemical 
disasters in Bhopal. The Government is aware about the tragic consequences of this disaster. 

Special  [30 APRIL 2008]  Mentions    175 
Even today, after 23 years, we are experiencing the  continuous environmental disaster in 
this area. Apart from immediate deaths of nearly 10 ,000 people within 72 hours, this has 
caused further estimated 18,000 to 20,000 deaths till today. Meanwhile, the population in 
this area is forced to consume groundwater contaminated with chemicals which cause birth 
defects, cancer and other health related problems. The Central Government, in the year 
2006, promised to rehabilitate the affected population and get the plant site cleansed of the 
9000 tonnes of chemical residues in Bohpal which continue to poison people, and take the 
long overdue legal action against Carbide and its successor, Dow Chemical Company. The 
Coordination Committee on Bhopal has been constituted and met three times in two years. 
But none of its recommendations has been implemented. Eight thousand tonnes of chemical 
waste is said to have been dumped under the ground which will create another disaster and 
environmental hazards. I request the Government to address issues of medical, economic, 
social and environmental rehabilitation and provide clean water for the affected population 
of Bhopal. 
Demand to sanction a revival package for Bharat Heavy Plates and Vessels 
Limited, Vishakhapatnam  
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY (Andhra Pradesh): The BHPV is one of the oldest industries 
set up in Visakhapatnam, which plays a vital role f or industrial growth in Visakhapatnam. 
Many auxiliary/ancillary industries have come up and they are continuously depending upon 
BHPV. The Company started production in 1971-72 with the turn over of Rs. 1.95 crores and 
crossed Rs. 300 crores in 1996-97 and contributed around Rs. 450 crores to national exchequer 
during the past 14 years and the company has an order of Rs. 400 crores as on 1.4.2006. 
The Company has been referred to BIFR on 23.6.2004 under Sick Industrial Companies 
Act. The Government of India has been considering various options. The staff and workers 
of the unit whose lives are solely dependent on thi s have been representing repeatedly in 
this regard. The State Government has requested the  Government of India for early 
consideration and issue favourable orders to help t he organisation in execution of present 
orders in time which will pave way for revival and future growth. 
I, therefore, urge the Government to kindly consider the request of Andhra Government. 
Concern over acute shortage of power being faced by the country  
SHRI S. ANBALAGAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, the power situation in the country presents a 
grim picture. During 2007-08, the deficit in total energy availability was 8.4 per cent and the 
deficit in power supply in terms of peak availability was 14.8 per cent. This is the national 
picture. Some States, especially Tamil Nadu, face more acute power shortage than others. 
Rural areas face power shutdown or hours together d aily. Population growth and 
development necessitates corresponding growth in power generation. But when we compare 
the percentage of growth of power production during the period April to December in the 
years 2006-07, we are pessimistic of the Government's plans to meet the future power needs 
of the country. During this period, growth of power generation declined from 7.5 per cent in 
2006 to 6.6 per cent in 2007. Growth in hydroelectric power declined by 4 per cent from 13.8 
per cent to 9.8 per cent. Decline in production of environment friendly hydro-electricity is 
not good for the country. Likewise, there is steep fall in production of nuclear power from 
3 per cent in 2006 to'minus 5.7 per cent in 2007. As per National Electricity Policy, 2005, a 
capacity addition of 78,577 megawatts was proposed for the Eleventh Five Year Plan. But 
only 7,263 megawatts of generation facilities have been commissioned so far. This is high 

176 Special  [RAJYASABHA]  Mentions  
time the Union Government took immediate steps to increase power generation in coordination 
with the State Governments and the private sector, so as to meet the power needs of this 
vast country. Our national capital of Delhi faces acute power shortage which has to be

Concern over mounting subsidies and their continued failure to Bridge 
Economic Disparities  
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA (Maharashtra): Sir, subsidized higher education, unrealistically 
low prices of petrol, diesel, LPG, kerosene, is a burden on the Government resources 
due to majority of the actual beneficiaries being comparatively well-off. The target 
segments-BPL population, small farmers, rural households, etc., do not get any relief. 
Subsidies on fertilizers are cornered by the rich farmers. Public Distribution System 
does not percolate to the intended poor beneficiaries as they have no ration cards for 
lack of fixed address; microscopic minority possessing ration cards, do not have money 
to purchase their weekly quota of food-grains on any one day of the week. The envisaged 
objectives sought to be achieved through nearly Rs. 1,00,000 crore subsidies are nowhere 
near fulfilment. The extant delivery system is replete with corruption, diversion of 
subsidized items, atrophied infrastructure assigned for the purpose, and unimaginative 
procedures.  
I do feel that all types of subsidies should not be tarred by the same brush. The National 
Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme is targeted towards the rural poor- the relatively well-
off will not enrol in such schemes. But a recent CAG report has castigated its working also. 
Therefore, effective new modalities seem to be the only solution. I therefore, urge upon the 
Government that through a collective wisdom of a Group of Ministers like Finance, Rural 
Development, Panchayati Raj, Consumer Affairs and PDS, Petroleum etc., a synergetic 
approach, based on interaction amongst implementing agencies, self-help groups with 
proven deep rural penetration and actual beneficiaries, may be devised. This may initially 
bring us towards fulfilment of the UPA Government's avowed aim to bring the economic 
disparities, and gradually, usher in an era of prosperity for aam admi.

Demand to take Effective measures for afforestation in the Country  
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, India is the second most populated 
and the seventh largest country in the world having a population of one billion with only 1.8 
per cent of the world forests.The forests of India are sustaining the needs of 16.7 per cent of 
the world's human and 18 per cent of livestock population. Forests contribute 1.7 per cent of 
the GDP of our country. Unfortunately, the desired objective to cover 33 per cent of our 
geographical area under trees is yet to be achieved. Even though the National Forest Policy of 
1952 and the new National Forest Policy of 1988 proposed that 60 per cent of me land in the 
hills and 20 per cent in the plains should be covered under forest.,But the net result is that 
we are having only 19.27 per cent of forest cover and.the.per caita forest is 0.08 per cent, 
comparing to Japan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines,and Sri Lanka, where 66.8 per \ cent, 
60.6 per cent, 47.1 per cent; 22.7.per cent and 27,8 percent forest cover are existing. The 
lack of proper forest cover will have a. serious impact on ecological, balance, in our 
country. Accoding to our estimates, India will be, at least, 3 degrees Celsius hotter by 2050. 
Many of the rivers will be dried; cyclones will be more intense, and there will be a severe 
water and food shortage. The Himalayan glaciers are also slowly melting and there will be a 
severe ecological imbalance. Hence, if we don't take immediate and urgent steps in this 
regard, then, we are bound to witness catastrophe. Hence, The Government of India should 
take it up on a war-footing basis and make it a great national movement.

increase. We have to stop the inflationary expectation as it may have effect on micro-
economic stability and it will create problems for us. But, Sir, in order to face that, if I am a 
market reformer, which, I think, I am, I will not try to tickle the market prices too much, 
reducing the import duty, changing the export duty, etc. It is all right if it can create an effect. 
The main solution will have to be monetary policy and the Reserve Bank of India may go 
into that. However, the most important point again from the Aam Aadmi's point of view is 
that inflation will be there, which we shall try to control. But when inflation is there, we must 
protect the poor people. Sir, poor and vulnerable people's consumption has to be protected. 
For that, we have to expand the Public Distribution System and the Public Distribution 
System has to be expanded both for BPL and APL categories because the APL category 
people are also very poor. They are not twelve rupees per capita, but twenty rupees per 
capita Consumption classes. There can be leakages. I am not saying that the system is leak-
proof. That is question of administration.  
We have to expand the Public Distribution System. Sir, I raised this issue day-before-
yesterday with Mr. Sharad Pawarji. He said, 'now the stocks are better, we shall consider 
whether we can actually do that. 'But, Sir, this is not the issue. When the stocks are better, 
definitely we should do. But even if the stocks are not good enough, your first requirement 
is to establish this Public Distribution System. For which, if you need to import you have to 
import. But you cannot import at this high price, you have to subsidise and that subsidy is 
most important. Yes, that day, there was an issue that was raised 'why not you procure from 
the market, from the farmers?' If that is possible, you should do that. ...(Time-bell)... I don't 
mind which is the source of your expenditure. But we must accept that the Public Distribution 
has to expand, has to be provided with funding, and, for that, adequate funds are necessary.  
Sir, the last point that I want to mention is that the Finance Minister has been very 
successful in managing the tax system. He has generated substantial revenue. He has 
generated revenue out of the growth process to which he has made some contribution. We 
must accept that. But, Sir, the last point is that with this revenue, what are you going to do? 
Are you going to give more tax concessions? Are you going to give more money to others? 
Or are you actually trying to use them up for the poor people? This is the question that has 
to be addressed. ...(Interruptions)... With these words, Sir. I conclude. ...(Interruptions)...

SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN (West Bengal): Sir, I rise to place my observation on the 
Finance Bill and related matters. At the outset, I would like to respond to only one of the many 
points raised by the hon. Leader of the Opposition so far as the role of the Planning Commission 
is concerned. 
[THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH) in the Chair] 
He expressed a very strong observation about the in effectiveness of the entire Planning 
Commission reaching almost to the stage of dismissing the need for planning altogether, as I 
could understand it. 
I have my strong criticism about the Planning Commission that they are doing everything except 
planning. That is, instead of reining in the conflicting interests and operations of their various 
economic agents in the economy, to ensure a proper allocation of resources as per the national 
priorities, they are floating along with the market rather along with the interests who dominates 
the market and dictates the market. But what is needed is not to dismiss the concept of planning 
altogether. It would be like throwing the baby out with bath water. What is important is.to bring the 
whole Planning Commission to sense that they need to moderate the entire market forces in favour of 
the people and to ensure the most equitable allocation of resources as per the national priorities. I 
think there lies the difference. 
I think the first issue is the vexed problem of con tinuing price rise and a sort^f evasive 
response on the part of the Government about their role to contain the same. The House has had 
a number of structured discussions on it. And every time, the Government claims, or, at least, 
asserted their claim that they have been taking corrective actions. But on the ground, those 
corrective actions through various monetary and fis cal instruments could cause very little 
influence in taming the rising prices. That is a reality, and now, at the end 

Government  [30APRIL2008]  Bills   199  
of the day, when a voice is being raised against that in this House and outside, the whole 
blame for the price rise and inflationary situation has been passed on to the international 
phenomenon on the one hand, and on the other hand. Government is casting a blame on 
those who are raising the voice against the price rise as scare monger or politicising the 
issue. I think, this is utterly an irresponsible st atement and a shocking response of the 
Government towards the most serious problem faced by our country. Very recently, Madam 
Condoleezza Rice sang a song in the same tune when she told that it is because of India and 
China. If you consider her statement as an international phenomenon, India and China are 
eating more, so the price of food is rising globally in this manner. I don't know. I want to get 
the response of the hon. Finance Minister to such an innovative and indeed brilliant statement 
of Madam Condoleezza Rice. No doubt, prices are rising globally. It is a fact. But any 
Government worth the name has some responsibility to guard its people against it. Instead of 
that, on the one side, the scare mongering blame is being put on those criticising it, and on 
the other hand, a mis-informed claim is being made that the inflation rate in India is the 
lowest in the world. I think, a very recent report of the 'Economist' ranked India 33 rd  in terms 
of annual rise in the consumer prices, and the developing countries like Malaysia, Hong 
Kong, South Korea, Slovakia, Mexico, Brazil, Span, Thailand etc. which are much more 
open to the global economic dynamism, have a much lower inflation rate than India. So, that 
claim is also not correct. The problem lies in\ the obsession of our policy-makers, to absolve 
the perpetrators of the price rise directly. The main perpetrator, as per my understanding, is 
the speculative forces playing in both the commodit ies and the financial market. The 
budgetary proposal and also the Finance Bill carefu lly sidetracked action on those 
perpetrators, the speculative forces which reflects their loyalty to the neo liberal economic 
philosophy; and that is why, the concrete proposal of the Left Parties to ban future trading on 
25 essential commodities, as recommended by the Parliament Standing Committee on Food 
and Consumers Affairs recently, and earlier by the Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Agriculture also, went completely unheeded. The demand for universalization of the Public 
Distribution System to take on the price rise, these are all measures to directly have an 
assault on the basic problem of price rise. When all other indirect instruments to contain the 
price rise through play of market forces, through different monetary and fiscal instruments 
completely failed during the , last few months, again and again, we discussed this issue in 
this House. So, the need of the hour is to have a direct assault through completely banning 
the future trading of all the 25 commodities, universalizing the PDS, reducing the prices of 
petrol and diesel, and also containing the private procurement of food-grains, making it 
mandatory to declare all stocks in food-grains in any godown from 10,000 tons onwards to 
contain black marketing and hoarding. These are the issues, and I think, the most urgent 
need of the hour is to tackle them on priority basis. We will request the Finance Minister as 
representing the Government to look into this very serious problem of the people and 
initiate certain actions by directly attacking the price rise. In this context, the very urgency 
of food subsidy and the universalization of the Public Distribution System have to be taken

is a very fine institution which was originally sug gested and conceived by Wanchoo 
Committee. It is probably the speediest way of coll ecting taxes because there is no appeal 
provided against the decision given by the Settleme nt Commission. If efficiency is lost 
because of poor implementation, but what is needed is proper implementation, proper manning 
of the people in that and seeing to it that right t ype of people are manning the Settlement 
Commission. Instead thereof, all pending matters lying before the Settlement Commission have to 
lapse by 31 st March, 2008. Hundreds of petitions have been filed. I myself am responsible for 
filing several petitions in Bombay High Court. As a result of these petitions large amount of 
taxes are now in limbo. The petitions will not be disposed of for a number of years. So, I would 
respectfully submit that instead of keeping this date as 31st March, 2008, let it be 31st March, 
2010. See to it that proper people are appointed and all pending matters are disposed of. This is 
very necessary. Another thing which I would like to mention, are provisions relating to Sikkim. It 
has been mentioned that some of the exemptions, which are given, are restricted to those who 
have got themselves registered under the Sikkim subjects register. But this register was never 
compulsory. There are a large number of people who are domiciled in Sikkim, enjoying the same 
rights and sharing the same rights, responsibilities as other citizens of Sikkim who have got 
themselves registered. I think, the exemption, which is given, should be made applicable to 
each and every one of them, not only those who have got themselves registered but those who are 
domiciled in Sikkim. Then, I have to say about the fringe benefit tax. The fringe benefit tax has 
probably given rise to a large amount of litigation. I believe that instead of fringe benefit tax we 
should go back to the old system of Section 37 where there was discounted deduction. If you 
have incurred some expenditure where recipient is not found, don't give deduction for entire 100 
per cent, give deduction only for 50 per cent. A 50 per cent deduction is given and an amendment 
in Section 37 will put an end to the entire chapter-relating to the fringe benefit tax. But recipient is 
not found. Identify the recipient. It is a simple thing. We take it in the hands of the recipient. 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: That provision was there. The complaint against that provision was, 
enormous discretion put in the hands of the assessing officers who could either disallow or 
not disallow. So when we move away from discretion to non-discretion you complain about 
the non-discretionary powers. 
SHRI Y.R TRIVEDI: I am saying that make it very clear. If the recipient is not found in 
whose hands it is to be taxed, you can find out the recipient, tax it in the hands of the recipient. 
If recipient is hot found, it is an expenditure on which you suffer a discounted deduction of 50 
per cent. Sir, these are the some of the ideas.

to Dalit community. Sir, there are certain issues a bout the working class where the Finance 
Ministry is not/directly concerned. Sometimes, we are told that disinvestment or SEZ or the

also appreciate and agree with me that one of the most important Ministries in the Government

At the same time, I congratulate the hon. Finance Minister for presenting one of the best
